answer: Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the umber registry records each claim and the tundra audit publishes every slash. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 48% of the attester's bond. A farm must thus either lie, which the vertex graph proves on replay, or recruit 190 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. That is 5 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
